id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-multipoint unidirectional broadcast — single transmitter ↔ up to 20 receivers on one shielded 78 Ω twisted-pair per direction.

supported_topologies.name: Single simplex bus
supported_topologies.description: One transmitter drives one shielded 78 Ω twisted-pair; up to 20 receivers tap onto the pair. Most messages are a single 32-bit data word.

supported_topologies.name: Bidirectional pair (two buses)
supported_topologies.description: Two simplex 429 buses between subsystems that exchange data both ways — one bus per direction.

supported_topologies.name: Per-equipment dedicated outbound bus
supported_topologies.description: Each transmitting subsystem typically owns one or more outbound buses; receivers subscribe to subsets of labels.

supported_topologies.name: ARINC 615 data-loader overlay
supported_topologies.description: Higher-layer data-loader protocol layered on top of ARINC 429 PHY.

supported_topologies.name: Replaced on newer airframes
supported_topologies.description: On Airbus A380 and Boeing 787, deterministic switched Ethernet (ARINC 664 Part 7 / AFDX) replaces 429 for most data links; 429 remains for legacy interfaces.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Single source on the bus; constantly emits 32-bit words or NULL; maintains label-table + per-label update-rate schedule.
Passive monitor; up to 20 per bus; runs local Label filter + parity check + SSM decode.
ARINC 429 has no contention or arbitration — only one transmitter per bus.

fields.interconnect_role: There is no protocol-layer interconnect, router, or bridge in ARINC 429. The bus is a flat shared simplex medium; any of the up-to-20 receivers can decode any word, and label-acceptance filtering is purely local at each receiver. Avionics integration concatenates many individual 429 buses (often dozens to hundreds per aircraft) into a star/mesh wired interconnect at the airframe level.

ordering_guarantees.single_bus: All receivers see every word simultaneously (modulo cable propagation); data consistency is automatic.
ordering_guarantees.no_arbitration: Words from one transmitter are emitted in the order the transmitter's scheduler interleaves them — typically a fixed priority-by-update-rate scheme.
ordering_guarantees.label_periodicity: Each label is transmitted at its nominal fixed update rate per equipment-type spec; receivers may rely on this cadence to detect transmitter-down conditions.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: Not applicable — ARINC 429 is wire-level. Per-controller register / FIFO / label-filter regions live in the device datasheet (Holt HI-3584, TI DEI1016, etc.), not in the ARINC 429 specification.

slave_classification.addressable_target: Not applicable — ARINC 429 is content-addressed by Label (octal). All up-to-20 receivers see every frame; selection is local Label-filter match.
slave_classification.data_producer: Exactly one transmitter per bus emits 32-bit words encoding labels assigned to that equipment type.
slave_classification.data_consumer: Up to 20 receivers per bus, each with its own Label-acceptance list.

default_signal_values_evidence_tables: Technical description — medium and signaling (BRZ on shielded 78 Ω twisted-pair).
Word format — bits 1-32 with Label / SDI / Data / SSM / Parity fields.
Bit numbering, transmission order, and bit significance — Bit 1 first on the wire.
Labels — equipment-type-specific octal assignments (ARINC 429 Part 1-17 Sections 78-116).
Protection from interference — RTCA DO-160 environmental compliance + cable shielding + balanced differential + BPRZ encoding.

wake_up_topology.wake_up_trigger: Not applicable — ARINC 429 has no sleep/wake-up state machine. The transmitter is continuously active (emitting NULL when idle).
wake_up_topology.post_wake_sync: Receivers continuously track BRZ transitions; they resynchronize automatically on every word's bit 1.
